```{python}
#| output: false
import sys
from pathlib import Path
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path.cwd()))
import json
import polars as pl
from IPython.display import display
from _guard import load, load_json, source


def ojs_define(**kwargs):
    """Hand the guarded data to OJS as a rendered sidecar.

    Quarto's python-to-OJS MIME bridge is undocumented and this Quarto build
    did not emit the tag, so the documented interface is used instead: the
    data is written beside the document and read as a FileAttachment, which
    `embed-resources` inlines into the self-contained page. The sidecar is a
    render artefact, gitignored; every value in it still arrived through the
    fail-closed guard above.
    """
    Path("_explore_data.json").write_text(json.dumps(kwargs))


series = load("data/build/series/province_series.csv")
st = load("data/build/series/zone_table_status.csv")
summ = load("data/build/series/province_summary.csv")
cav = load("data/build/series/provisional_caveat.csv")
lab = load("data/build/series/lab_prose.csv")
meta = load_json("data/build/streams/meta.json")
comp = load("data/build/compare/zone_comparison.csv")
ex = source("registers/reconciliation_exceptions.tsv")

caveats = (cav.filter(pl.col("kind") == "recent_data_provisional")
           .select("sitrep", "date"))
route = dict(st.select("sitrep", "table").iter_rows())
cavset = set(caveats["sitrep"])
exset = set(ex["sitrep"].cast(pl.Int64))

cum = (series.filter(pl.col("cum_cases").is_not_null())
       .sort(["province", "date"])
       .with_columns((pl.col("cum_cases") - pl.col("cum_cases").shift(1)
                      .over("province")).alias("inc"))
       .with_columns(
           pl.col("sitrep").map_elements(lambda s: route.get(s, "—"),
                                         return_dtype=pl.Utf8).alias("route"),
           pl.col("sitrep").is_in(cavset).alias("caveat")))

rings = (summ.filter((pl.col("level") == "province")
                     & pl.col("cum_cases").is_not_null())
         .with_columns(pl.col("zone_reported").str.strip_chars("*†‡ ")
                       .alias("province"))
         .select("sitrep", "date", "province", "cum_cases"))

streams_long = []
for slug, prov in (("ituri", "Ituri"), ("nord_kivu", "Nord-Kivu"),
                   ("haut_uele", "Haut-Uélé")):
    for kind in ("cases", "deaths"):
        d = load(f"data/build/streams/{kind}_{slug}.tsv")
        for r in d.iter_rows(named=True):
            streams_long.append({"time": r["time"], "province": prov,
                                 "kind": kind,
                                 "count": r[f"{kind}_{slug}"]})

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path.cwd().parent / "scripts"))
from aggregate_provinces import carry_province  # noqa: E402

panel = carry_province(load("data/build/series/zone_table.csv"))
date2rep = dict(st.select("date", "sitrep").iter_rows())


# The one smoother, imported -- a copy here drifted from the figure's once
# already (the copy clipped negative revisions to zero inside the window,
# which manufactured the right skew the residual section then reported).
from plot_figures import _roll_geomean  # noqa: E402


def _smooth(vals, days, window=7, max_gap=4):
    xs = [d.toordinal() for d in days]
    return _roll_geomean(xs, vals, window=window, max_gap=float(max_gap))


import datetime as _dt
flows_long = []
for prov in ("Ituri", "Nord-Kivu"):
    per = {}
    base = (series.filter((pl.col("province") == prov))
            .sort("date"))
    for col, name in (("cum_cases", "cases_diff"), ("cum_deaths", "deaths_diff")):
        b = base.filter(pl.col(col).is_not_null())
        vals = (b[col] - b[col].shift(1)).to_list()[1:]
        per[name] = list(zip(b["date"].to_list()[1:], vals))
    blk = (panel.filter((pl.col("province") == prov)
                        & pl.col("level").is_in(["zone", "unassigned"])))
    for col in ("new_cases", "deaths_community", "deaths_treatment_centre"):
        b = (blk.filter(pl.col(col).is_not_null())
             .group_by("date").agg(pl.col(col).sum()).sort("date"))
        per[col] = list(zip(b["date"].to_list(), b[col].to_list()))
    lb = (lab.filter(pl.col("province") == prov)
          .group_by("date").agg(pl.col("samples").sum()).sort("date"))
    if lb.height:
        per["lab_tests"] = list(zip(lb["date"].to_list(),
                                    lb["samples"].to_list()))
    for name, rows in per.items():
        days = [_dt.date.fromisoformat(d) for d, _ in rows]
        sm = _smooth([v for _, v in rows], days)
        for (d, v), m in zip(rows, sm):
            flows_long.append({"stream": name, "province": prov, "date": d,
                               "sitrep": date2rep.get(d), "value": v,
                               "smooth": m})

index_rows = [
    {"report": r["sitrep"], "date": r["date"], "route": r["table"] or "—",
     "rows": r["rows"], "identity": r["identity"] or "—",
     "residual": r["residual"],
     "flags": ", ".join(
         (["caveat"] if r["sitrep"] in cavset else [])
         + (["exception"] if r["sitrep"] in exset else []))}
    for r in st.sort("sitrep").iter_rows(named=True)]

ojs_define(
    cumJ=cum.select("sitrep", "date", "province", "cum_cases", "cum_deaths",
                    "inc", "n_parts", "route", "caveat").to_dicts(),
    ringsJ=rings.to_dicts(),
    caveatsJ=caveats.to_dicts(),
    streamsJ=streams_long,
    compJ=comp.to_dicts(),
    indexJ=index_rows,
    flowsJ=flows_long,
)
```

This page is the interactive companion to the data document. Everything you
see here is read from the pipeline's built files at the moment the page is
rendered, and every read goes through the same guard the data document uses:
if a file isn't one the pipeline declares and actually produces, the render
stops rather than quietly showing you something stale.

The data come from INSP's daily situation reports (sitreps), the numbered
bulletins the national public health institute publishes during the outbreak.
Some of those reports warn that their most recent figures are still being
consolidated and may change. I mark each of those reports with a faint pink
vertical line; the "show consolidation caveat" toggle above turns them off.
Hover over any point to see which report it came from.

## Cumulative confirmed cases by province

A health zone is the DRC's basic unit of health administration, smaller than a
province, and most reports print a table with one row per zone. The line here
is what you get when I add up those zone rows for each province. That sum is
the series everything else on this site is built from.

Many reports also print their own subtotal row for each province, and those
are the open rings. Because the ring and the line come from the same page,
they should land on top of each other. When a ring sits off its line, the
report's own arithmetic doesn't add up, and that's worth looking into.

```{ojs}
{
  const sel = cum.filter(d => provinces.includes(d.province));
  const selR = rings.filter(d => provinces.includes(d.province));
  return Plot.plot({
    width: 950, height: 430, marginLeft: 55,
    color: {...colorScale, legend: true},
    y: {type: logy ? "log" : "linear", grid: true,
        label: "cumulative confirmed cases"},
    x: {label: null},
    marks: [
      showCaveat ? caveatMarks() : null,
      Plot.lineY(sel, {x: "day", y: "cum_cases", stroke: "province",
                       strokeWidth: 1.8}),
      Plot.dot(sel, {x: "day", y: "cum_cases", fill: "province", r: 2.4,
        channels: {report: "sitrep", route: "route",
                   "zone rows summed": "n_parts", "deaths": "cum_deaths",
                   "source flags provisional": "caveat"},
        tip: true}),
      Plot.dot(selR, {x: "day", y: "cum_cases", stroke: "province", r: 4.5,
        symbol: "circle", fill: "none",
        channels: {report: "sitrep", "printed summary value": "cum_cases"},
        tip: true}),
    ]
  });
}
```

## New cases between consecutive reports

Each point is one report, placed at its reporting date, and shows how much the
cumulative count went up since the report before it. I haven't smoothed or
adjusted anything here. A zero means the report printed the same cumulative as
the previous one, so those zeros are really in the data. A point below zero
means the source revised its cumulative downward, and I've left those in too.

```{ojs}
{
  const sel = cum.filter(d => provinces.includes(d.province) && d.inc != null);
  return Plot.plot({
    width: 950, height: 380, marginLeft: 55,
    color: {...colorScale, legend: true},
    y: {type: logy ? "symlog" : "linear", grid: true,
        label: "new confirmed cases since previous report"},
    x: {label: null},
    marks: [
      showCaveat ? caveatMarks() : null,
      Plot.ruleY([0], {stroke: "#bbb"}),
      Plot.dot(sel, {x: "day", y: "inc", fill: "province", r: 3,
        channels: {report: "sitrep", route: "route"}, tip: true}),
    ]
  });
}
```

## Every daily series, by province

This is the interactive version of the grid of daily series in the data
document. Each row is one series I extract, and Ituri and Nord-Kivu, the two
main provinces of the outbreak, share that row's vertical scale. The grey
points are the numbers as each report published them. The coloured line is a
seven-day rolling geometric mean, the same smoother as in the static figure,
and it breaks wherever there's a gap in reporting so it doesn't draw a level
across days the source said nothing about.

The reference project also reads series from report tables I haven't fully
extracted yet: the laboratory, alerts, contact-tracing and isolation tables.
They'll show up here as rows once I do.

```{ojs}
//| output: false
flows = flowsJ.map(d => ({...d, day: parseD(d.date)}))
FLOW_LABELS = new Map([
  ["cases_diff", ["Confirmed cases / day", "differenced cumulative — the fitted stream"]],
  ["new_cases", ["New confirmed cases / day", "the source's own 24 h figure, printed from 13 July"]],
  ["deaths_diff", ["Confirmed deaths / day", "differenced cumulative"]],
  ["deaths_community", ["Community deaths / day", "post-mortem swab — the ascertainment signal"]],
  ["deaths_treatment_centre", ["Treatment-centre deaths / day", "the other half of the same split"]],
  ["lab_tests", ["Samples analysed / day", "laboratory prose — every point licensed by its own printed positivity"]],
])
```

```{ojs}
{
  const provs = ["Ituri", "Nord-Kivu"].filter(p => provinces.includes(p));
  if (provs.length === 0) return html`<em>Select Ituri or Nord-Kivu above.</em>`;
  const panels = [...FLOW_LABELS].map(([key, [title, sub]]) => {
    const sel = flows.filter(d => d.stream === key && provs.includes(d.province));
    if (sel.length === 0) return null;
    const plot = Plot.plot({
      width: 950, height: 190, marginLeft: 55,
      color: colorScale,
      fx: {domain: provs, label: null},
      y: {type: logy ? "symlog" : "linear", grid: true, label: null},
      x: {label: null},
      marks: [
        showCaveat ? caveatMarks() : null,
        Plot.ruleY([0], {stroke: "#ddd"}),
        Plot.dot(sel, {fx: "province", x: "day", y: "value", r: 2,
          fill: "#a5a5a5",
          channels: {report: "sitrep", stream: () => title}, tip: true}),
        // The nulls in `smooth` ARE the gap-breakers -- Plot leaves a gap at
        // an invalid y, so they must reach the mark, not be filtered out;
        // filtering them reconnects the line across the reporting gaps it
        // exists to break.
        Plot.lineY(sel, {fx: "province", x: "day", y: "smooth",
                         stroke: "province", strokeWidth: 1.7}),
      ]
    });
    return html`<div style="margin-bottom:0.4rem">
      <div style="font-size:0.86rem"><b>${title}</b>
        <span style="color:#777"> — ${sub}</span></div>
      ${plot}</div>`;
  });
  return html`${panels}`;
}
```

## How noisy is the reporting?

Here I take each report's number and ask how far it sits from the smoothed
line. Since the smoother averages on a log scale, I measure the distance on
that scale too, as `log1p(observed) − log1p(smoothed)`. Pay more attention to
the shape of the histogram than to its mean. The smoothing window includes the
point being measured and gets cut short at the start and end of the series, so
the residuals won't be centred exactly on zero.

What would a real problem look like? If reports were batched, with a run of
reports that undercount followed by one that catches up all at once, you'd see
a strong right skew. Still, be suspicious of any lopsidedness you see here. An
earlier version of this page showed Ituri skewed at +0.62, and all of it came
from two of the source's downward revisions. The smoother was treating them as
zeros, which pulled the line down and pushed every nearby residual up. Once
those revisions are left out properly, both provinces come out close to
symmetric. So negative increments are kept out of the histogram and out of
every smoothing window, and I count them in the note above the plot instead.

```{ojs}
viewof resStream = Inputs.select(
  ["cases_diff", "deaths_diff", "new_cases"],
  {label: "stream", format: k => FLOW_LABELS.get(k)[0]})
```

```{ojs}
{
  const provs = ["Ituri", "Nord-Kivu"].filter(p => provinces.includes(p));
  if (provs.length === 0) return html`<em>Select Ituri or Nord-Kivu above.</em>`;
  const base = flows.filter(d => d.stream === resStream
                            && provs.includes(d.province)
                            && d.smooth != null && d.value != null);
  const neg = base.filter(d => d.value < 0);
  const res = base.filter(d => d.value >= 0)
    .map(d => ({...d, res: Math.log1p(d.value) - Math.log1p(d.smooth),
                weekday: d.day.toLocaleDateString("en", {weekday: "short", timeZone: "UTC"})}));
  const stats = provs.map(p => {
    const r = res.filter(d => d.province === p).map(d => d.res).sort(d3.ascending);
    return {province: p, n: r.length,
            median: d3.median(r), mean: d3.mean(r),
            above: r.filter(v => v > 0).length / r.length};
  });
  const hist = Plot.plot({
    width: 950, height: 300, marginLeft: 55,
    color: colorScale,
    fx: {domain: provs, label: null},
    x: {label: "log1p(observed) − log1p(smoothed)"},
    y: {label: "reports", grid: true},
    marks: [
      Plot.rectY(res, Plot.binX({y: "count"},
        {x: "res", fx: "province", fill: "province", thresholds: 25,
         tip: true})),
      Plot.ruleX([0], {stroke: "#555"}),
      Plot.ruleX(stats, {x: "median", fx: "province", stroke: "#555",
                         strokeDasharray: "3,3"}),
    ]
  });
  // Pre-aggregated in plain JS rather than via Plot's group transform: the
  // medians are the statement, so they are computed once, inspectably, and
  // the mark receives seven numbers per province -- nothing left for a
  // transform to render weirdly.
  const DAYS = ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"];
  const wkMed = provs.flatMap(p => DAYS.map(day => {
    const vs = res.filter(d => d.province === p && d.weekday === day)
                  .map(d => d.res);
    return {province: p, weekday: day, n: vs.length,
            median: vs.length ? d3.median(vs) : null};
  })).filter(d => d.median !== null);
  const wk = Plot.plot({
    width: 950, height: 220, marginLeft: 55,
    color: colorScale,
    fx: {domain: provs, label: null},
    x: {domain: DAYS, label: null},
    y: {label: "median residual", grid: true},
    marks: [
      Plot.ruleY([0], {stroke: "#999"}),
      Plot.barY(wkMed, {fx: "province", x: "weekday", y: "median",
        fill: "province",
        channels: {"reports that weekday": "n"}, tip: true}),
    ]
  });
  const line = stats.map(s =>
    `<b>${s.province}</b>: n=${s.n}, median ${s.median.toFixed(3)}, ` +
    `mean ${s.mean.toFixed(3)}, ${(100 * s.above).toFixed(0)}% above the line`)
    .join(" · ");
  const negline = neg.length
    ? `<br><span style="color:#a33">${neg.length} negative increment(s) — ` +
      `the source's own downward revisions — excluded from the histogram.</span>`
    : "";
  return html`<div>
    <div class="note">${line}${negline}</div>
    ${hist}
    <div class="note" style="margin-top:0.8rem">Median residual by weekday —
    a consistent weekday dip or bump is a reporting-cycle artefact, not
    epidemiology.</div>
    ${wk}</div>`;
}
```

## The weekly series downstream models fit

These are exactly the series that downstream models read, taken from
`data/build/streams/`. Counts are binned by week, and by the last week each
series has no gap left against the printed cumulative totals.

When the source revises its cumulative downward, the drop has to go
somewhere. I don't publish it as a negative weekly count, and I don't throw it
away either. Instead I carry the deficit forward and take it out of the weeks
that follow. That way every bar is a whole number of zero or more, and each
series still adds up to the full change in the printed cumulative.
`data/build/streams/revisions.tsv` lists every row that this correction
changed. The solid bars are cases and the paler bars drawn over them are
deaths.

```{ojs}
{
  const sel = streams.filter(d => provinces.includes(d.province));
  return Plot.plot({
    width: 950, height: 170 * Math.max(1, new Set(sel.map(d => d.province)).size),
    marginLeft: 55,
    color: {...colorScale},
    fy: {label: null},
    y: {grid: true, label: "weekly count"},
    x: {label: "week ending"},
    marks: [
      Plot.rectY(sel.filter(d => d.kind === "cases"),
        {x: "day", interval: "week", y: "count", fy: "province",
         fill: "province", fillOpacity: 0.9,
         channels: {week: "time", kind: "kind"}, tip: true}),
      Plot.rectY(sel.filter(d => d.kind === "deaths"),
        {x: "day", interval: "week", y: "count", fy: "province",
         fill: "province", fillOpacity: 0.4,
         channels: {week: "time", kind: "kind"}, tip: true}),
      Plot.ruleY([0]),
    ]
  });
}
```

## My extraction against INRB-UMIE's, zone by zone and day by day

INRB-UMIE, at the national laboratory, publishes its own transcription of the
same situation reports. I don't build anything from it; I only compare
against it. Each point is one health zone in one report, with their number on
one axis and mine on the other. Keep in mind that both of us are reading the
same pages. When we agree, that tells you we copied the numbers correctly. It
doesn't tell you anything about whether the counts themselves are right. A
red point is a place where we disagree, and you can hover over it to see the
full record.

```{ojs}
{
  const ok = comp.filter(d => !d.disagree && d.cum_cases > 0 && d.inrb_cases > 0);
  const bad = comp.filter(d => d.disagree);
  return Plot.plot({
    width: 500, height: 480, marginLeft: 55,
    x: {type: "log", label: "INRB-UMIE transcription", grid: true},
    y: {type: "log", label: "this extraction"},
    marks: [
      Plot.lineY([{x: 1, y: 1}, {x: 5000, y: 5000}],
                 {x: "x", y: "y", stroke: "#ccc"}),
      Plot.dot(ok, {x: "inrb_cases", y: "cum_cases", r: 1.6, fill: "#c9c9c9"}),
      Plot.dot(bad, {x: "inrb_cases", y: "cum_cases", r: 5, fill: "#D55E00",
        channels: {zone: "zone_reported", report: "sitrep", date: "date",
                   "ours": "cum_cases", "INRB": "inrb_cases",
                   "Δ cases": "diff_cases", "Δ deaths": "diff_deaths"},
        tip: true}),
    ]
  });
}
```

## Every report, in one table

You can search this table and sort it by any column. *Route* is the table
layout I read that report's zone counts from, since the reports changed format
over the course of the outbreak. *Identity* records whether the page's own
arithmetic holds: `ok` if the zone rows add up to the totals the report prints,
`fails` if they don't. *Residual* is the size of the gap when they don't.
Under *flags*, `caveat` means the report warns its recent figures are still
being consolidated, and `exception` means I've checked the mismatch by hand
against the page and recorded it in `registers/reconciliation_exceptions.tsv`.

```{ojs}
viewof q = Inputs.search(indexJ, {placeholder: "filter reports…"})
```
```{ojs}
Inputs.table(q, {rows: 30, maxWidth: 950,
  columns: ["report", "date", "route", "rows", "identity", "residual", "flags"]})
```
